claims.text: Kubernetes supports upgrading a cluster by one minor version at a time; skipping minor versions is unsupported, so a cluster two minor versions behind needs two upgrades in a row. The kubeadm upgrade guide covers one minor step and calls skipping unsupported.
Version skew: kubelet must not be newer than kube-apiserver and may be up to three minor versions older (for kubelet 1.25 and later); so the control plane is upgraded before the nodes.
kubectl is supported within one minor version, older or newer, of kube-apiserver. The upgrade guides install the new kubectl after the control plane.

kubeadm upgrade apply, on the first control-plane node, checks the cluster is upgradeable (API server reachable, all nodes Ready, control plane healthy), enforces the version skew policies, then upgrades the control-plane components (static Pods).
kubeadm upgrade automatically renews the certificates it manages on the node it upgrades.

kubeadm upgrade node: on additional control-plane nodes it upgrades the static Pod manifests and the kubelet configuration; on workers it updates the kubelet configuration. kubeadm does not install the kubelet: it is upgraded as a separate step, then the kubelet is restarted.

claims.text: Control-plane nodes are upgraded one node at a time; each node, control plane included, is drained before its kubelet minor upgrade and uncordoned after (in-place minor kubelet upgrades without drain are not supported).

Worker order: upgrade kubeadm, run kubeadm upgrade node, drain, upgrade and restart the kubelet, uncordon. Workers go one or a few at a time without compromising the capacity workloads need; afterwards kubectl get nodes shows Ready and the new version.
A node's Ready condition is True when the node is healthy and ready to accept Pods.

If all nodes are drained at once, evicted Pods have no schedulable node; with a PodDisruptionBudget the API server refuses further evictions and the drains keep retrying, without one all Pods are evicted.

claims.text: Old API versions are deprecated and eventually removed: each release lists the API versions it stops serving, and manifests and API clients must be migrated to a served version; cluster-upgrade.md lists adjusting manifests as an upgrade step.

Check manifests, charts and operators against the target version and take an etcd snapshot before an upgrade starts; the kubeadm docs advise backups because kubeadm upgrade only touches Kubernetes' own components.

claims.text: Each node reports its kubelet version in status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion; version-skew.sh prints kubectl version (dropping the Kustomize line) and that column plus the container runtime for every node, and upgrades nothing. Runtime and Kustomize versions are not part of the version skew policy.
